title: Do loyalty programs pay?
paragraphs: Retail analysts often credit loyalty programs with raising customer spending. Yet a closer reading of the data suggests a different order of events: customers who already spend heavily are the ones most likely to join, so the programs may simply identify big spenders rather than create them. A grocery chain tested this by offering membership to a random half of its shoppers. Members' spending rose only slightly, far less than the gap between members and non-members in the chain's earlier records. This result does not show that loyalty programs are worthless, since they may yield other benefits, such as better data on shopper preferences, but it does undercut the simplest account of how they work.
